The king defends marriage as the gods' own joy, leaves the outcome to destiny, loads her with gifts and lutes, and consoles himself that daughters, like the conch's pearls, are for others; she leaves the grieving palace and boards the aerial car.
source_issues: Verse 545 line 3: நின்ணை has ண் where நின்னை is expected; probably a typing slip.
Verse 550 line 2 repeats the phrase அருமணிக் கொடிகொல் மின்கொல் of 549 line 2 (here யருமணிக் கொடிகொன் மின்கொ) and ends cut off; the line looks disturbed or contaminated from the verse before.
Verse 557 lines 3-4: சினந்தலை மழுங்கல் இன்றி and குருமணி முடியிற் றேய்த்த தரன்றமர் are hard to divide and may be corrupt.
Verse 562 line 4: வேந்தன் னாற்றுகி லாது doubles the ன்.
Verse 564 line 4: the text flag reports a repaired ோ் read as ேர்.

cast.role: the Vidyadhara king of Vichaloka in Gandhara on the silver mountain, Gandharvadattai's father
the merchant (நாய்கன்), Civakan's friend, received by the Vidyadhara king
daughter of the Vidyadhara king, mistress of the vina, to be won by a contest of music
the Vidyadhara king's queen, Gandharvadattai's mother
Gandharvadattai's companion, charged to go with her
the gatekeeper of the Vidyadhara king's palace
the women who fan the Vidyadhara king with yak-tail whisks
Gandharvadattai's mothers (mother and foster mothers)
Gandharvadattai's companions
a Vidyadhara of the king's people (named in 557)

tamil: பால்பரந் தன்ன பட்டார் பூவணை பசும்பொற் கட்டிற்
கால்பரந் திருந்த வெங்கட் கதிர்முலை கச்சின் வீக்கி
வேல்பரந் தனைய கண்ணார் வெண்மதிக் கதிர்பெய் கற்றை
போலிவர் கவரி வீச மன்னவ னிருந்த போழ்தின்.
reading: The narrator sets the scene: the king sits on a couch of fresh gold spread with silk soft as milk, while women with spear-like eyes and breasts bound in bodices wave whisks white as the moon's rays.
event: The Vidyadhara king sits at ease on his couch, fanned by women with whisks.

tamil: என்வர விசைக்க வென்ன வாயிலோ னிசைப்ப வேகி
மன்னர்தம் முடிகள் வேய்ந்த வயிரம்போழ்ந் துழுது சேந்த
பொன்னவிர் கழல்கொள் பாதம் பொழிமழைத் தடக்கை கூப்ப
வின்னுரை முகமன் கூறித் தானத்தி லிருக்க வென்றான்.
reading: The guest asks the gatekeeper to announce him, enters and joins his hands before the king's gold-anklet feet, reddened by the diamonds of bowing kings' crowns, and the king greets him with sweet words and bids him take a seat.
nuance: Who says என்வரவு இசைக்க is not stated; the merchant is the likeliest, but the Vidyadhara who brought him could be meant. The feet that kings' crowns have scored with diamonds make the welcome a condescension from a king of kings.
event: Sridattan is announced by the gatekeeper, bows before the Vidyadhara king, and is welcomed and seated.

tamil: முதிர்பெயன் மூரி வான முழங்கிவாய் விட்ட தொப்ப
வதிர்குரன் முரச நாண வமிர்துபெய்ம் மாரி யேய்ப்பக்
கதிர்விரி பூணி னாற்குத் தந்தைதாய் தாரங் காதன்
மதுரமா மக்கள் சுற்றம் வினவிமற் றிதுவுஞ் சொன்னான்.
reading: In a voice like ripe thunder that shames the war drum and falls like a rain of nectar, the king asks the jewelled merchant after his father, mother, wife, sons and kin, and goes on to say more.
nuance: The voice is thunder and nectar at once: the king's majesty and his kindness are given in a single simile, preparing the speech that will level king and merchant.
event: The Vidyadhara king asks after Sridattan's family.

tamil: இன்றைய தன்று கேண்மை யெமர்நும ரெழுவர் காறு
நின்றது கிழமை நீங்கா வச்சிர யாப்பின் னூழா
லன்றியு மறனு மொன்றே யரசன்யான் வணிக னீயே
யென்றிரண் டில்லை கண்டாய் யிதுநின தில்ல மென்றான்.
reading: The king tells the merchant that their bond is not of today: kinship between his people and the merchant's has held for seven generations, bound by fate in an unbreakable diamond tie, and since their dharma is one there is no 'I a king, you a merchant'; this is his own house.
nuance: Two grounds are given for the friendship, ஊழ் and a shared அறம், and the second dissolves rank: the king of the Vidyadharas sets aside the difference of station in so many words. Whether அறன் here means a shared religion or a shared code of conduct the verse does not say.
event: The Vidyadhara king declares an old family friendship with Sridattan and makes him at home.

tamil: மந்திர மன்னன் சொன்னீர் மாரியால் வற்றி நின்ற
சந்தனந் தளிர்த்த தேபோல் சீதத்தன் றளிர்த்து நோக்கி
யெந்தைக்குத் தந்தை சொன்னா னின்ணை மென்று கேட்ப
முந்தைத் தான் கேட்ட வாறே முழுதெடுத் தியம்புகின்றான்.
reading: At the king's words Sridattan revives like a sandal tree withered by drought that puts out shoots in the rain, and when he asks whether it was his grandfather who spoke of the king, the king recounts in full what he had heard of old.
nuance: The sense of line 3 is not certain: எந்தைக்குத் தந்தை சொன்னான் நின்னை may be the merchant's question (did my grandfather speak of you?) or part of the king's answer; and who tells the tale in line 4 is not named.
event: Sridattan, revived, asks about the old tie, and the king begins to tell its history.

tamil: வெள்ளிவே தண்டத் தங்கண் வீவில்தென் சேடிப் பாலிற்
கள்ளவிழ் கைதை வேலிக் காசில்காந் தார நாட்டுப்
புள்ளணி கிடங்கின் விச்சா லோகமா நகரிற் போகா
வெள்ளிவேற் கலுழ வேகன் வேதண்ட வேந்தர் வேந்தன்.
reading: The tale begins: on the southern row of the silver mountain, in the faultless land of Gandhara with its screwpine hedges, in the great city of Vichaloka girt by a moat full of birds, ruled Kaluzhavegan of the silver spear, king of the kings of the mountain.
nuance: வெள்ளி வேதண்டம் and its southern row (தென் சேடி) place the Vidyadhara realm in the Jain cosmic geography. Whether Kaluzhavegan names himself here or an ancestor of the line is not clear from the verse.

tamil: சங்குடைந் தனைய வெண்டா மரைமலர்த் தடங்கள் போலும்
நங்குடித் தெய்வங் கண்டீர் நமரங்கா ளறிமி னென்னக்
கொங்குடை முல்லைப் பைம்போ திருவடங் கிடந்த மார்ப,
விங்கடி பிழைப்ப தன்றா லெங்குல மென்று சொன்னான்.
reading: Pointing to pools of white lotuses like broken conch, the speaker says 'these are our clan deities, our people, know it', and declares that their clan does not stray from these feet.
nuance: The verse nests a speech within a speech (என்ன ... என்று சொன்னான்), and the referent of இங்கு அடி, the feet the clan never fails, is not given; it may be the clan deity or the old pledge to the merchant's line.

tamil: பெருந்தகைக் குருசி றோழன் பெருவிலைக் கடக முன்கை
திருந்துபு வணங்கப் பற்றிச் சென்றுதன் னுரிமை காட்டப்
பொருந்துபு பொற்ப வோம்பிப் பொன்னிழை சுடர நின்ற
கருங்கண்ணி திறத்து வேறாக் கட்டுரை பயிற்று கின்றான்.
reading: Taking the bracelet-adorned forearm of the noble prince's friend as he bowed, the king leads him into his inner quarters, shows him the dark-eyed girl who stands guarded and shining in gold, and begins to speak of her in a new strain.
nuance: பெருந்தகைக் குருசில் தோழன் makes the merchant Civakan's friend, linking this distant court to the hero before he appears. Showing a guest the உரிமை, the women's apartments, is itself the proof of the intimacy the king has just claimed.
event: The king leads Sridattan into the women's quarters and shows him his daughter.

tamil: எரிமணிப் பளிக்கு மாடத் தெழுந்ததோர் காம வல்லி
யருமணிக் கொடிகொன் மின்கொ லமரர்கோ னெழுதி வைத்த
வொருமணி குயின்ற பாவை யொன்று கொலென்று நாய்கன்
றிருமணிக் கொடியை யோரான் றெருமர மன்னன் சொன்னான்.
reading: The merchant cannot tell whether he sees a creeper of desire risen in the crystal mansion, a vine of rare gems, lightning, or a jewelled doll painted by the king of the gods, and as he stands bewildered the king speaks.
nuance: The run of questions with கொல் is the akam device of the man who cannot decide whether the woman is human (compare the Kural's அணங்குகொல்), given here to a merchant who looks on her as a father's guest, not a lover.
event: Sridattan is bewildered at the sight of the princess.

tamil: தூசுலாய்க் கிடந்த வல்கு றுப்புறழ் தொண்டைச் செவ்வாய்
வாசவான் குழலின் மின்போல் யருமணிக் கொடிகொன் மின்கொ
யூசல்பாய்ந் தாடிக் காதிற் குண்டல மிலங்க நின்றாள்
காசில்யாழ்க் கணங்கொள் தெய்வக் காந்தர்வ தத்தை யென்பாள்.
reading: The king names her: she who stands with her garment slipping on her hips, coral-red mouth and fragrant hair, flashing like lightning, her earrings shining as she leaps from the swing, is Gandharvadattai, the divine one who holds the throng of faultless lutes.
nuance: Line 2 repeats words from 549 line 2 and ends cut off; the description may be disturbed.
event: The king names his daughter Gandharvadattai to the merchant.

tamil: விளங்கினா ளுலக மெல்லாம் வீணையின் வனப்பி னாலே
யளந்துணர் வரிய நங்கைக் கருமணி முகிழ்த்த வேபோ
லிளங்கதிர் முலையு மாகத் திடங்கொண்டு பரந்த மின்னிற்
றுளங்குநுண் ணுசுப்புந் தோன்றா துரவரு வென்ன வுண்டே.
reading: Her fame lights the whole world through the beauty of her vina playing; she is a girl past measuring, whose young breasts swell like budding dark gems and whose slender waist, fine as lightning, cannot be seen at all, though it must exist.
nuance: Her renown is for her art before her beauty: the vina, the instrument of the contest to come, is named first. Whether this is still the king speaking or the narrator is not marked.

tamil: நின்மக ளிவளை நீயே நின்பதிக் கொண்டு போகி
யின்னிசை பொருது வெல்வா னியாவனே யானு மாக
வன்னவற் குரிய ளென்ன வடிப்பணி செய்வ லென்றான்
reading: The king tells the merchant to take this girl, now called the merchant's own daughter, to his city: whoever defeats her in a contest of sweet music shall have her, even if it be himself, and he will serve that man at his feet; the queen, hearing it, says this is fitting for Dattai.
nuance: நின்மகள் transfers the daughter to the merchant in a word: she leaves as his child. The condition 'even if I be the one' (யானும் ஆக) makes the contest absolute, binding the king himself, and the queen's consent is recorded as a separate act.
event: The king entrusts Gandharvadattai to Sridattan, to be given to whoever beats her at music, and the queen consents.

tamil: முனிவரும் போக பூமிப் போகம்முட் டாது பெற்றுந்
தனியவ ராகி வாழ்தல் சாதுய ரதனி னில்லை
கனிபடு கிளவி யார்தங் காதலர் கவானிற் றுஞ்சிற்
பனியிரு விசும்பிற் றேவர் பான்மையிற் றென்று சொன்னான்.
reading: The king says that even with the tireless pleasures of the land of enjoyment granted without fail, there is no misery like living alone, while to sleep in the lap of a lover sweet of speech is the very state of the gods in the cool sky.
nuance: போக பூமி is the Jain cosmology's land of enjoyment, where couples are born together; the king uses a Jain heaven to argue for marriage. முனிவரும் is better taken as முனிவு அரும் (pleasures one never tires of) than as 'even sages'.

tamil: நூற்படு புலவன் சொன்ன நுண்பொரு ணுழைந்தி யானும்
வேற்கடற் றானை வேந்தர் வீழ்ந்திரந் தாலு நேரேன்
சேற்கடை மதர்வை நோக்கிற் சில்லரித் தடங்க ணங்கை
பாற்படு காலம் வந்தாற் பான்மையார் விலக்கு கிற்பார்.
reading: The king says that, having grasped the subtle meaning of what the learned seer foretold, he would not give her even if kings with armies like the sea fell at his feet and begged; when the destined time for this wide-eyed girl comes, who can stop those it is destined for?
nuance: Fate here does not defeat a plan; it is the king's reason for refusing all suitors and leaving the outcome to the contest. The seer (நூற்படு புலவன்) is mentioned but his prophecy is not told in this verse.

tamil: படைப்பருங் கற்பி னாடன் பாவையைப் பரிவு நீக்கிக்
கொடைக்குரிப் பால வெல்லாங் கொடுத்தபின் கூற்று முட்கும்
விடைப்பருந் தானை வேந்தன் வேண்டுவ வெறுப்ப நல்கித்
தொடுத்தலர் கோதை வீணா பதிக்கிது சொல்லி னானே.
reading: The king of an army that even Death fears puts off his grief for his daughter of matchless chastity, gives all the things proper to a bride's giving and more than was wanted, and says this to Veenapathi, her garlanded companion.
nuance: பரிவு நீக்கி: the giving is done only after the father masters his grief, and the dowry is called கொடைக்குரிப்பால, what belongs to the act of giving away.
event: The king gives his daughter's dowry and turns to Veenapathi.

tamil: உடம்பினொ டுயிரிற் பின்னி யொருவயி னீங்கல் செல்லா
நெடுங்கணுந் தோளும் போலு நேரிழை அரிவை நீநின்
றடங்கணி தனிமை நீங்கத் தந்தையுந் தாயு மாகி
யடங்கல ரட்ட வேலா னாணையி ராமி னென்றான்.
reading: The king tells Veenapathi that she and the princess are like eye and shoulder, woven together as body and life and never apart; she must be father and mother to the girl so that she never feels alone, and both must live under the command of the spear-bearer who slew his foes.
nuance: The spear-bearer of line 4 is unnamed; it may be the merchant, now her guardian, or the king's own authority. The charge 'be her father and mother' answers the king's claim in 553 that living alone is the worst misery.
event: The king charges Veenapathi to be a parent to Gandharvadattai.

tamil: அருமணி வயிரம் வேய்ந்த வருங்கலப் பேழை யைஞ்ஞூ
றெரிமணி செம்பொ னார்ந்த விராயிரம் யவனப் பேழை
திருமணிப் பூணி னாற்குச் சினந்தலை மழுங்க லின்றிக்
குருமணி முடியிற் றேய்த்த தரன்றமர் கொள்க வென்றான்.
reading: The king orders five hundred chests set with rare gems and diamonds and two thousand Yavana chests full of red gold and blazing gems to be carried for the jewelled merchant by Dharan's people.
nuance: சினந்தலை மழுங்கல் இன்றி and குருமணி முடியில் தேய்த்த are hard to construe; 'Dharan's people' depends on dividing தரன்றமர் as தரன் தமர்.
event: The king sends chests of gems and gold with the merchant.

tamil: பல்வினைப் பவளப் பாய்காற் பசுமணி யிழிகை வம்பார்
நல்லகில் விம்மு கட்டி றவிசொடு நிலைக்கண் ணாடி
மெல்லிய தூப முட்டி மேதகு நானச் செப்போ
டல்லவுங் கொள்க வென்றா னணங்குடை நிணங்கொள் வேலான்.
reading: The king of the fat-smeared spear adds couches of worked coral with gem-set legs and fragrant aloe, seats, standing mirrors, soft incense, caskets of musk and more.
event: The king adds furniture, mirrors and perfumes to the gifts.

tamil: விளக்கழ லுறுத்த போலும் விசியுறு போர்வைத் தீந்தேன்
றுளக்கற வொழுகி யன்ன துய்யறத் திரண்ட திண்கோல்
கொளத்தகு திவவுத் திங்கட் கோணிரைத் தனைய வாணி
யளப்பருஞ் சுவைகொ ணல்யா ழாயிர மமைக வென்றான்.
reading: He orders a thousand fine lutes of boundless sweetness, their skin covering taut as if warmed by lamp-flame, their stems smooth as flowing honey, their frets set like a row of moons.
nuance: The last and fullest gift is the vina, the instrument of the contest: a thousand of them go with her, as if the music that will decide her marriage travels as her dowry.
event: The king gives a thousand lutes.

tamil: அரக்கெறி குவளை வாட்க ணவ்வளைத் தோளி னாளைப்
திருப்புறக் கொடுத்த செம்பொற் றாமரை போன்று கோயில்
புரிக்குழன் மடந்தை போகப் புலம்பொடு மடிந்த தன்றே
reading: Her loving mothers embrace the girl of sword-sharp lily eyes again and again, and as she leaves like a red-gold lotus turning its back, the palace sinks in grief.
event: Gandharvadattai's mothers embrace her and the palace grieves as she departs.

tamil: காம்புபொன் செய்த பிச்சங் கதிர்மணி குடையொ டேந்தித்
தாம்பலர் கவரி வீசக் கிண்கிணி ததும்ப நாகப்
பாம்புபைத் தனைய வல்குற் பல்கலை மிழற்ற வேகி
யாம்பனா றமுதச் செவ்வா யரசனைத் தொழுது நின்றாள்.
reading: With parasols of jewelled rays on golden poles and many whisks waving, her anklets jingling and her girdle chiming, she goes and stands with folded hands before the king.
event: Gandharvadattai goes in state and bows before the king.

tamil: அடிக்கல மரற்ற வேகி யரும்பெறற் றாதை பாத
முடிக்கலஞ் சொரியச் சென்னி யிறைஞ்சலு முரிந்து மின்னுக்
கொடிப்பல நுடங்கி யாங்குத் தோழியர் குழாத்து ணிற்ப
வடுத்தனன் புல்லி வேந்தன் னாற்றுகி லாது சொன்னான்.
reading: Her anklets sounding, she bows her head at her father's feet so that her ornaments spill, and stands among her companions like a cluster of swaying lightning-creepers, and the king, unable to bear it, embraces her and speaks.
event: Gandharvadattai bows at her father's feet, and he embraces her in grief.

tamil: வலம்புரி பயத்தை எய்தா தனையரே மகளி ரென்ன
நலம்புரிந் தனைய காதற் றேவிதன் னவையை நீங்கக்
குலம்புரிந் தனைய குன்றிற் கதிபதி கூறி னானே.
reading: The lord of the mountain says that daughters are like the pearl a right-whorled conch bears, which benefits those on the earth and never the conch, and with this he consoles the queen as she leaves the assembly.
nuance: Line 3 (தேவி தன் அவையை நீங்க) can be read as the queen leaving the assembly or as the king dispelling the queen's sorrow; either way the saying is said to console, so it turns a loss into the order of things.
event: The king consoles the queen with a saying on daughters as the princess departs.

tamil: இன்சுவை யாழொ டன்ன மிளங்கிளி மழலை மஞ்ஞை
பொன்புனை யூக மந்தி பொறிமயிர்ப் புறவம் பொன்னார்
மென்புன மருளி னோக்கின் மானின மாதி யாகத்
தன்புறஞ் சூழப் போகித் தளிரியல் விமானஞ் சேர்ந்தாள்.
reading: Surrounded by sweet lutes, swans, lisping young parrots, peacocks, golden monkeys, spotted doves and herds of deer with timid eyes, the tender girl goes and reaches the aerial car.
event: Gandharvadattai leaves with her pets and lutes and boards the aerial car.

title: காந்தருவதத்தையார் இலம்பகம் 565-588 (4/15)
theme: Gandharvadattai is carried through the sky with a vast army whose elephants out-roar the clouds; Dharan reveals to Sridattan that his shipwreck was a ruse made at Kaluzhavegan's bidding after an astrologer's word, shows him his ship and companions safe, and Sridattan brings the princess home to Rajamapuram, tells his wife, and gains the king's consent for her marriage rite.
source_issues: 565-576 and 578-580 are short-line verses printed two lines to a line in the source; the tool split them into four lines.
577 survives as two long lines (stanza_length flag): its four short lines were printed in pairs separated by '!' and ',' and were not split; the text itself seems whole.
588 line 4: a TSCII slip (ோ் for ேர்) repaired in நேர்ந்தான்.

cast.role: a merchant of Rajamapuram, friend of the vidyadhara king
the vidyadhara who staged Sridattan's wreck and brought him to the Silver Mountain
the vidyadhara king of the Silver Mountain, Gandharvadattai's father
Kaluzhavegan's astrologer
kings who sought Gandharvadattai on the Silver Mountain
the vidyadhara princess
Sridattan's companions on the ship
Sridattan's wife
the usurping minister, now ruling Rajamapuram as king

reading: The only daughter of the victorious vidyadhara king sets out, moving with a great army as her retinue.
event: Gandharvadattai sets out from the Silver Mountain with a great armed retinue.

reading: Her escort counts a thousand elephants rejoicing at the eye's edge and twice that number of chariots that move through the sky.
Horses in golden trappings, able to turn back an army of bowmen, go with her in a number multiplied over the troops already named.
nuance: The count in நற்புடைய நாற்றியே is not clear: it may be fourfold the chariots or simply a great many.

reading: Young warriors bearing sun-bright spears that the vultures follow, twelve thousand of them, beyond telling, march in the train.
When the clouds thunder in the high sky, the elephants trumpet back at them, and the clouds, shaken, cannot pass on.
nuance: Who is shaken and cannot go on (அதிர்ந்தவர்க்கு ஏகலாவது இல்லையே) is not fixed by the words; it may be the clouds or anyone who hears.

reading: At the roaring of the furious elephants the clouds split their bellies and shed their water in fear.
nuance: The army's passage through the sky is made into a storm: the rain is the clouds' terror at the elephants, not weather.

reading: The elephants' ichor, mingled with the falling rain, pours down into the deep sea, inside and out.
The poet turns to tell what befell the rich man who had grieved when his ship capsized in the wide sea.
nuance: The narrator's 'let us tell' (செப்புவாம்) closes the description of the flight and returns to Sridattan, last seen at Kaluzhavegan's court.

reading: The milk-white snowy mountain shines whiter still, with gems of blue shadow set in rows all through it.
nuance: The verse does not say what it describes; it may be the Silver Mountain the party leaves, or the shining place where the ship is now shown.

reading: The great vidyadhara, to the delight of the guileless man's heart, makes known to him that the whole wreck was a deception.
nuance: The man deceived is called வஞ்சமின் மனத்தினான், one with no deceit in his mind, in the same verse that names the deceit (வஞ்சம்); the pun sets the guileless merchant against the vidyadhara's ruse.
event: Dharan reveals to Sridattan that the shipwreck was a trick he staged.

reading: Dharan tells him that because of the maiden's beauty kings with conch-sounding armies thronged everywhere on the cloud-capped Silver Mountain.
event: Suitor kings throng the Silver Mountain for Gandharvadattai.

reading: The king, with dripping garland, spear and ஆர் flowers on his chest, takes counsel with the astrologer of generous hand, who speaks with grace.
nuance: Which of the two செப்பினான் makes the speaker, the king or the astrologer, is not settled by the line; the next verse is the astrologer's answer.
event: Kaluzhavegan consults his astrologer about his daughter's marriage.

reading: The astrologer declares that the maiden's life lies on the earth, and that therefore the king's beloved friend is even now out on the sea.
nuance: These words are the astrologer's, quoted inside Dharan's report. Who நின் காதலான் is cannot be fixed from this verse alone; 578's 'my close friend' suggests Sridattan, the man who will take her to the earth. The verse survives as two long lines.

reading: When the astrologer had spoken, Dharan says, the king bade him go and bring his dear friend, and that is how he came that day.
event: Kaluzhavegan sends Dharan to fetch Sridattan.

reading: Since there is no joy except for those who have first suffered, Dharan says, he bound Sridattan in suffering out of love.
nuance: The maxim is offered as a deceiver's apology: the suffering was made on purpose, for the joy it would set off. The work does not comment on it here.

reading: Saying that he had gained his friend by causing him pain and wishing him long life, Dharan points out the ship he had sunk in the great sea and the companions in it.
event: Dharan shows Sridattan the sunken ship and his companions, safe.

tamil: தேன்றரு மாரி போன்று திவ்விய கிளவி தம்மா
லூன்றரு குருதி வேலா னுள்ளகங் குளிர்ந்து விஞ்சைக்
கோன்றரு துன்பம் மற்றென் குலத்தொடு முடிக வென்றான்
கான்றுவில் வயிரம் வீசும் கனமணிக் குழையி னானே.
reading: Cooled within by Dharan's divine words, like rain that brings honey, the spear-bearer with heavy gem earrings answers with a wish that the suffering the vidyadhara lord gave be brought to its end with his own line.
nuance: The wish கோன்தரு துன்பம் மற்றென் குலத்தொடு முடிக may mean that such suffering end here, or that a suffering bringing such gain stay with his line to its end; the words allow both.
event: Sridattan answers Dharan graciously.

tamil: தோடலர் தெரிய லான்றன் றோழரைக் கண்டு காத
லூடலர்ந் தெழுந்து பொங்க வுருவத்தார் குழையப் புல்லிப்
பாடிரும் பௌவ முந்நீர்ப் பட்டது பகர்த லோடு
நாடக நாங்க ளுற்ற தென்றுகை யெறிந்து நக்கார்.
reading: Seeing his friends, Sridattan embraces them with love welling up until his garland is crushed; they tell what they went through on the sea and, clapping their hands, laugh that it was all a play.
nuance: நாடகம் turns the wreck that drowned all aboard (512) into a staged show, and the laughter (நக்கார்) comes after the danger, not in it.
event: Sridattan embraces his companions, who laugh that their wreck was a play.

tamil: கட்டழற் கதிய புண்ணிற் கருவரை யருவி யாரம்
பட்டது போன்று நாய்கன் பரிவுதீர்ந் தினியர் சூழ
மட்டவிழ் கோதை யோடு மண்கனை முழவ மூதூர்க்
கட்டவிழ் தாரி னான்றன் கடிமனை மகிழ்ந்து புக்கான்.
reading: Like a mountain waterfall poured on a burning wound, the merchant's grief is quenched, and with his dear ones around him and the garlanded maiden he joyfully enters his guarded house in the old city of drums.
event: Sridattan comes home to Rajamapuram with Gandharvadattai.

tamil: பெருமனை குறுக லோடும் பிறையென விலங்கித் தோன்றுந்
திருநுதன் மனைவி செம்பொற் கொடியென விறைஞ்சி நிற்ப
வருமுலை பொதிர்ப்ப வாங்கி வண்டின மிரியப் புல்லிக்
கதிர்நகை முறுவன் மாதர் கண்ணுறு கவலை தீர்த்தான்.
reading: As he nears the great house his wife, her brow shining like the crescent, stands bowing like a golden creeper; he raises her, embraces her and takes away the worry from her eyes.
event: Sridattan embraces his wife and ends her anxiety.

tamil: சந்திர காந்த மென்னுந் தண்மணி நிலத்தி னங்கண்
வெந்தெரி பிசும்பொன் வெள்ளி பளிங்கொடு பவளம் பாய்த்திக்
கந்தெரி மணியிற் செய்த கன்னியா மாட மெய்திப்
பைந்தொடிப் பாவை யொன்றும் பரிவிலள் வைகி னாளே.
reading: The maiden comes to the maidens' mansion built on a floor of cool moonstone with gold, silver, crystal and coral, its pillars set with gems, and dwells there without distress.
event: Gandharvadattai is lodged in the maidens' mansion.

tamil: பாசிழைப் பரவை யல்குற் பசுங்கதிர்க் கலாபம் வீங்கக்
காசுகண் பரிய வைகிக் கடன்றலைக் கழிந்த பின்னாத்
தூசணி பரவை யல்குற் றுளங்குநுண் ணுசுப்பிற் பாவை
யாசறு வரவும் தந்தை வலித்தது மறியச் சொன்னான்.
reading: After the household duties are done, Sridattan tells his wife, so that she knows it, of the faultless maiden's coming and of what her father has resolved.
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 describe a woman resting till her duties are done; whether she is the wife or the maiden, and so to whom Sridattan speaks, depends on reading பாவை in line 3 against the subject of வைகி.
event: Sridattan tells his wife of Gandharvadattai's arrival and her father's purpose.

tamil: வண்டுண மலர்ந்த கோதை வாயொருப் பட்டு நேரத்
தெண்கட லமிர்தம் பெய்த செப்பெனச் செறிந்து வீங்கிப்
பெண்டிரு மாண்மை வெஃகிப் பேதுறு முலையி னாளைக்
கண்டவர் மருள நாளைக் கடிவினை முடித்து மென்றான்.
reading: His wife consents, and he says that next day they will carry through the rite for the girl whose breasts make even women covet manhood, so that all who see her marvel.
nuance: கடிவினை is the rite that leads to her marriage; the verse does not yet name the lute contest.
event: Sridattan's wife consents and he resolves to begin the marriage rite next day.

tamil: மால்வரை வயிறு போழ்ந்து வல்லவர் மதியிற் றந்த
பால்வரை மணியும் பொன்னும் பற்பல கொண்டு புக்குக்
கால்பொரு கழலி னானுங் காவலற் கண்டு சொன்னான்
வேல்பொரு தானை யானும் வேண்டுவ விதியி னேர்ந்தான்.
reading: Taking much gold and many gems that skilled men had cut from the mountain's belly, the anklet-wearer goes in, sees the ruler and tells him; the king of the spear army grants what he asks, as rule allows.
nuance: The verse does not name the king; at this point of the story Rajamapuram's ruler is the usurper Kattiyangaran, and his consent is bought with gems.
event: Sridattan brings gifts to Kattiyangaran and gains his consent to what he asks for Gandharvadattai.

title: காந்தருவதத்தையார் இலம்பகம் 589-612 (5/15)
theme: With the king's leave, the merchant Sridattan has ten thousand workers build a hall of gold and crystal for the vina contest, which the poet praises at length; drummers proclaim through the city a Jain benediction, a call to give to ascetics and do penance, and the terms by which Tattai will go to whoever of the three classes surpasses her at the vina, and the first suitor kings arrive.
source_issues: 590 line 2: மண்டபங்செய் is irregular sandhi (expected மண்டபஞ்செய்); read as 'build a hall'.
600 line 4: the division புக்கயா வுயிர்த்த is doubtful.
606 line 2 and 608 line 1: the core repaired TSCII slips (ோ் for ேர், ௌ for ெள); the repaired readings are used.
610 line 3: வேழத்தத்தின புரத்து fuses வேழத்து and அத்தினபுரத்து.
611 line 4: பாலமா குமரன் may be a name or 'the young prince'; the division is uncertain.

cast.role: merchant of Rajamapuram, foster-father of Gandharvadattai on the Vidyadhara king's trust
the usurping minister, now ruling Rajamapuram as king
the Vidyadhara princess, here proclaimed as the merchant's daughter
the ten thousand workers who build the contest hall
the young men Sridattan sends to the drummers
the drummers who proclaim the vina contest through the city
king of Hastinapuram, a suitor
king of Kampili, a suitor
king of Varanavasi, a suitor

reading: The king of the musth-elephant ranks is pleased, and the merchant of unfailing fame, his garland opened by pressing breasts, goes off glowing with joy, reaches his house quickly and gives the order to begin.
nuance: The king who consents here is the usurper Kattiyangaran, so the contest that will bring Civakan his first bride is held by leave of the man who killed his father.
event: Kattiyangaran approves the merchant's request, and Sridattan hurries home and orders the work begun.

reading: He orders a hall of fine gold, fit to be set in the sky, built in the midst of the moated city, and the reckoners fix its time: the month of Meenam, Friday, the tithi Jaya, the bright fortnight, when the vengai blooms in the forest.
nuance: The time is fixed by sign, weekday, tithi and fortnight, with the vengai's flowering as the seasonal mark; who reckons it (கண்ணினர்கள்) is not named.
event: Sridattan orders a gold hall built in the city, and its auspicious time is fixed.

reading: Ten thousand workers, friend, foe and those held in awe alike, are given fields that yield gold, silk, cotton cloth, fresh gold and food sweet with forest honey, and without a word set to their labour together.
nuance: Reading நட்புப்பகை யுட்கினொடு as the workers' range, friends, enemies and the fearful, all drawn in by the wages, is a guess at a compressed line.
event: Ten thousand workers are paid in land, cloth, gold and food and labour on the hall.

reading: Drinking toddy with its bee-sought fragrance, they break the ground deep with picks, level it to suit all eight directions, and over it lay a floor of melted gold that delights the eye.
event: The workers dig, level and lay a gold floor for the hall.

reading: They set gold pillars, shaped like stacked gold pots, firmly in the fresh gold floor, lay coral beams, spread crystal slats, roof it well and build the walls of red gold.
event: The workers raise gold pillars, coral beams, a crystal ceiling and gold walls.

reading: Where the maiden is to sit they raise walls of crystal, hang strings of cool pearls with garlands meeting garlands, and so adorn it that one would call it a temple for painters.
nuance: ஆலயம் இது ஓவியர்கட்கு makes the hall a shrine for the painters, the place their art is worshipped in, not a place of worship.
event: The workers build and adorn the crystal seat where the maiden will sit.

reading: Gold garlands with fine petals sway in the wind and bend near the doors like lightning in the rain-cloud, so that the hall shows even to the far-off like a tilakam, and sea-pearls are spread there as sand.
Elephants, she-elephants, calves, stags, lotus pools and birds are painted with lifelike grace beside figures and yakshis, so that viewers cannot tell which is inside and which outside.
nuance: The doubt (ஐயம்) whether painted creatures are inside the hall or out is the poet's praise of the painting as indistinguishable from the world.

reading: Even those who toiled on it look and are filled with joy; birds and beasts will not come near, as if it might swallow them; flags rise and dance, and nothing like it exists within the sea-fenced world: such is this fair mansion.

Tearing the running clouds and setting the shining moon on its crest, the mansion is like the long-haired lord with the crescent; with its four faces it is like four-faced Brahma; in its towering height it is like Nemi.
nuance: The building is compared in turn to the god who wears the moon in his matted hair, to Brahma and to the god of the wheel; a Jain epic by tradition uses the Vedic gods here only as measures of form and height, and claims nothing about them.

reading: Making all who see it desire it, it is like Kama; praised by the whole world, it is like the victorious king; and like the nectar of a woman's breasts, it is to each who enjoys it just what that person is.
nuance: The last line turns the praise inward: the hall's beauty is not one thing but answers the nature of whoever looks, as the woman's nectar does.

tamil: முகிற்றலை மதிய மன்ன முழுமணி மாடத் திட்ட
வகிற்புகை தவழ்ந்து வானத் தருவிசும் பறுத்து நீண்டு
பகற்கதிர்ப் பரப்பிற் றாகிப் பஞ்சவர் விமான முட்டிப்
புகற்கரு மமரர் கற்பம் புக்கயா வுயிர்த்த தன்றே.
reading: The agil smoke laid in the jewelled mansion, like the moon above the clouds, creeps up, cuts through the sky, spreads like daylight rays, touches the vimanas of the five and enters the kalpa heavens of the gods, who breathe it in.
nuance: கற்பம் and பஞ்சவர் விமானம் read as the heavens of Jain cosmology, the kalpas and five higher abodes; the word division of புக்கயா வுயிர்த்த is doubtful.

reading: Having taken leave by the king's grace and reached his broad house, the merchant, so that the world may know the manner of the announcement, sends swift young men as ordered to have the drum beaten through the old city.
event: Sridattan sends messengers to have the drummers proclaim the contest through the city.

reading: The messengers, swift as a loosed arrow and fearsome, reach the place where the drummers live and tell them to beat the thundering drum in the guarded city whose flags rise to touch the moon.
event: The messengers order the drummers to beat the proclamation drum.

reading: The drummers, in auspicious ornaments, open with the wish that the dharma path of the Excellent One may flourish in splendour, and then say they will proclaim the decree concerning the maiden with gem-bright smile and fragrant hair.
nuance: புங்கவன் அறநெறி names the path of the Excellent One, a title of the Jina; the public proclamation of a bride-contest is opened as a Jain benediction.
event: The drummers begin the proclamation with a blessing on the Jina's path.

tamil: வான்றரு வளத்த தாகி வையகம் பிணியிற் றீர்க
தேன்றரு கிளவி யாருங் கற்பினிற் றிரித லின்றி
யூன்றுக வூழி தோறு முலகினுண் மாந்த ரெல்லா
மீன்றவர் வயத்த ராகி யில்லறம் புணர்க நாளும்.
reading: May the world have the wealth the sky gives and be free of disease; may all honey-voiced women hold to chastity without swerving, firm through every age; may all people, obedient to those who bore them, practise the household dharma every day.
nuance: The rain, health, women's chastity and the household life are wished together as the goods of one well-kept world; the verse does not make any one of them the cause of another.

tamil: தவம்புரிந் தடங்கி நோற்குந் தத்துவர்த் தலைப்பட் டோம்பிப்
பவம்பரி கெமக்கு மென்று பணிந்தவ ருவப்ப வீமி
னவம்புரிந் துடம்பு நீங்கா தருந்தவ முயன்மின் யாருஞ்
சிவம்புரி நெறியைச் சேரச் செப்புமிப் பொருளுங் கேண்மின்.
reading: Seek out and care for the ascetics who practise penance in self-control, and give so that they rejoice, bowing and wishing that birth may be ended for you too; all of you, strive at hard penance while still in the body; and hear this matter proclaimed, so that you reach the path that leads to bliss.
nuance: The school is given as Jain because the proclamation opens on the Jina's path (603); the words here (தவம், பவம், சிவம் புரி நெறி) are shared with other schools. உடம்பு நீங்காது is read as 'before the body leaves', i.e. in this life; it could also mean 'without deserting the body'.

tamil: அம்மல ரனிச்சத் தம்போ தல்லியோ டணியி னொந்து
விம்முறு நுசுப்பு நைய வீற்றிருந் தணங்கு சேர்ந்த
வெம்முலைப் பரவை யல்குன் மிடைமணிக் கலாபம் வேய்த்தோட்
செம்மலர்த் திருவின் சாயற் றேமொழி தத்தை யென்பாள்.
reading: There is one called Tattai, sweet of speech, with the grace of the goddess of the red lotus, whose waist aches even under anicham flowers and whose jewelled girdle lies on her broad hips.

tamil: மற்றவ டந்தை நாய்கன் வண்கைச்சீ தத்தன் என்பான்
கொற்றவன் குலத்தின் வந்தான் கூறிய பொருளி தாகும்
கற்றவள் கணங்கொள் நல்யா ழனங்கனைக் கனிக்கும் நீராள்.
reading: Her father is the merchant Sitattan of the generous hand, who has come of a victorious line; this is what he has declared: she, rich in former penance, has learned all the arts of the great treatises and plays the fine yaazh so that she melts even Kama.
nuance: The proclamation names the merchant as her father, though he is her guardian on the Vidyadhara king's trust; her skill is credited to முற்றவம், past penance, as well as to learning. கொற்றவன் குலத்தின் வந்தான் may instead mean he came from the king's presence.

tamil: தீந்தொடை மகர வீணைத் தெள்விளி யெடுப்பித் தேற்றிப்
பூந்தொடி யரிவை தன்னிற் புலமிகுத் துடைய நம்பிக்
கீந்திடு மிறைவ ராதி மூவகைக் குலத்து ளார்க்கும்
வேந்தடு குருதி வேற்கண் விளங்கிழை தாதை யென்றான்.
reading: To the man of any of the three classes, kings first among them, who draws and makes clear the sweet notes of the makara vina with more skill than this bangled maiden, her father will give her: so the drummer cried.
nuance: The contest is open to the three classes headed by kings, so a merchant's son is not shut out; the bride goes to whoever surpasses her in music, not to the highest born.

tamil: மண்ணக மடந்தை யாக மார்புற முயங்கி நின்ற
வண்ணலை யாதி யாக வருங்கடி நகரை வாழ்த்தி
விண்ணக முழக்கி னேய்ப்ப வீதிதொ றெருக்கி யெங்குங்
கண்ணொளிர் கடிப்பி னோச்சிக் கடிமுர சறைந்த காலை,
reading: Blessing first the lord who embraces the earth-goddess as his bride, and then the guarded city, the drummers go through every street, beating the drum with gleaming sticks so that it thunders like the sky.
event: The drummers bless the king and the city and beat the drum through every street.

tamil: வணக்கருந் தானை மன்னர் மத்தகம் பிளந்து வாய்த்த
நிணக்கொழுங் குருதி வாட்கை நிலம்புடை பெயர்க்கு மாற்ற
கணைக்கவி னழித்த வுண்கட் கன்னியைக் கருதி வந்தான்.
reading: The king of Hastinapuram, whose sword hand drips the fat and blood of unbowing kings split at the brow and whose strength could shift the earth, comes with his hard-to-hold elephants, thinking of the maiden whose eyes shame arrows.
event: The king of Hastinapuram arrives seeking the maiden.

tamil: சிதைப்பருஞ் சீற்றத் துப்பின் செய்கழ னரல வீக்கி
மதக்களி றடர்த்துக் குன்ற மணிவட்டி னுருட்டு மாற்றற்
கதக்களி யொளிறு வைவேற் காம்பிலிக் காவல் மன்னன்
பதைப்பரும் பரும யானைப் பாலமா குமரன் வந்தான்.
reading: The guardian king of Kampili, of unbreakable wrath, who binds sounding anklets, subdues musth elephants and could roll a mountain like a gem-ball, comes, a prince with tall armoured elephants.
nuance: பாலமா குமரன் is read as 'the young prince' describing the king of Kampili; it may be a name.
event: The king of Kampili arrives for the contest.

tamil: இலைபொர வெழுதி யன்ன வெரிமணிக் கடக முன்கைச்
சிலைபொரத் திரண்ட திண்டோட் சில்லரிச் சிலம்பி னார்த
முலைபொர வுடைந்த தண்டார் மொய்ம்மதுத் துளிப்ப வந்தான்
மலைபொர வரிய மார்பின் வாரண வாசி மன்னன்.
reading: The king of Varanavasi comes, with jewelled bracelet on his forearm, shoulders like bows, a chest no mountain could match, and his cool garland, crushed against the breasts of anklet-wearing women, dripping honey.
event: The king of Varanavasi arrives for the contest.

title: காந்தருவதத்தையார் இலம்பகம் 613-636 (6/15)
theme: Suitor kings and crowds of every rank gather in Rajamapuram for the vina contest for Gandharvadattai; the merchant prepares the way and gives wealth away at the hour an omen-reader fixes, her companion predicts the suitors' defeat, attendants bathe and adorn her, and she goes out with auspicious emblems, the victor's garland, dwarfs and armed women guards, through a crowd whose eyes will not be held back by the guards.
source_issues: 623 line 3, 624 line 3, 625 line 1 and 636 lines 2 to 4 carry the repaired TSCII slip (ோ் read as ேர்) that show flags; the repaired forms read sensibly.
617 line 4 (நிலவரைத் தன்ன னாரை நிதியினால் வறுமை செய்தான்) is obscure as divided; the sense of gifts ending want is a reading.
618 line 1 (மண்டல நிறைந்த மாசின் மதிப்புடை வியாழம் போன்றோர்) is unclear as to whom it describes.
The metre changes at 631 (short lines through 635) and again at 636 (long lines); no rubric marks the changes.

cast.role: daughter of the Vidyadhara king Kaluzhavegan, whose hand goes to whoever beats her at the vina
merchant of Rajamapuram (நாய்கன்) who brought her from the Vidyadhara city and holds the contest
the woman with whom the merchant consults on the day, taken as his wife
the merchant's people who prepare the way to the contest hall
kings who came seeking the princess
the crowned king of Avanti, a suitor
the lord of the Ayodhya people, a suitor
everyone on earth, down to the rich merchants, who comes to try the vina contest
the crowds of Rajamapuram who come to watch
Gandharvadattai's companion
the reader of omens and planets who fixes the hour of the contest
the young women who bathe and dress the princess
the dwarfs and hunchbacks of the princess's retinue
the armed women of her guard, a thousand and eight

tamil: கதிர்முடி மன்னர் சூழ்ந்து கைதொழு திறைஞ்சி மாலைத்
திருமுடி வயிர வில்லாற் சேவடி திளைப்ப வேத்தி
யருமுடி யணிந்த கொற்றத் தவந்தியன் முரச மார்ப்ப
வொருபிடி நுசுப்பி னாளை யுள்ளுபு வந்து விட்டான்.
reading: Surrounded by kings who bow with joined hands, his crowned head praised, the victorious king of Avanti arrives to his drums, his mind on the maiden of slender waist.
event: The king of Avanti arrives at Rajamapuram for the vina contest, thinking of the princess.

tamil: வெள்ளணி யணிந்த ஞான்றே வேந்தர்தம் முடியிற் கொண்ட
கள்ளணி மாலை மோந்து கனைகழ லிலங்கும் நோன்றாட்
புள்ளணி கொடியி னானிற் போர்பல தொலைத்த வாற்ற
லள்ளிலை யணிந்த வைவே லயோத்திய ரிறையும் வந்தான்.
reading: The lord of the Ayodhya people, who on his coronation day sniffed garlands taken from kings' crowns and has won many battles with his leaf-bladed spear, comes too.
nuance: The suitors are introduced by their war record, so the coming contest of the lute is set against a field of conquerors whose strength it will not test.
event: The king of Ayodhya arrives for the contest.

tamil: நீணிதி வணிக ரீறா நிலமிசை யவர்க ளெல்லாம்
வீணையிற் பொருது வெல்வான் விரைவினர் துவன்றி மூதூர்க்
கோணமு மறுகு மெல்லாங் குச்சென நிரைத்தம் மாந்தர்
மாண்மது நசையின் மொய்த்த மதுகர வீட்ட மொத்தார்.
reading: Everyone on earth, down to the merchants of great wealth, hurries to win her at the vina, and the people crowd every corner and street of the old city in rows like swarms of bees drawn by honey.
nuance: The contest is open to anyone, merchants included, not only kings: this is what lets a merchant's son win it.
event: Suitors of every rank and crowds of townspeople throng the city.

tamil: உருக்கமைந் தெரியுஞ் செம்பொ னோரைவில் லகல மாகத்
திருக்குழன் மடந்தை செல்லத் திருநிலந் திருத்திப் பின்னர்,
விரைத்தகு நான நீரால் வெண்ணிறப் பொடியை மாற்றிப்
பரப்பினர் படுவண் டார்ப்பப் பன்மலர் பக்கம் எல்லாம்.
reading: For the maiden to walk on, they level a path five bows wide, lay down molten-bright gold, wash away the white dust with scented water and strew flowers loud with bees along its sides.
nuance: The word ஓரைவில் (five bows) as a measure of the path's width is read across the printed word break.
event: The way to the contest hall is levelled and laid with gold and flowers.

tamil: விலைவரம் பறித லில்லா வெண்டுகி லடுத்து வீதி
அலர்தலை யனிச்சத் தம்போ தைம்முழ வகல மாகப்
பலபடப் பரப்பிப் பாவை மெல்லடிப் பரிவு தீர
நிலவரைத் தன்ன னாரை நிதியினால் வறுமை செய்தான்.
reading: He spreads white cloth beyond price and soft anicham blossoms along the street to the width of five drums so her soft feet are spared, and with his wealth he makes the needy of the land, many as the earth, forget want.
nuance: Line 4, நிலவரைத் தன்ன னாரை நிதியினால் வறுமை செய்தான், literally says he made poverty for them by wealth; the sense that his gifts ended their want is a reading, and the subject is taken from the story.
event: The merchant carpets the street with cloth and flowers and scatters wealth.

tamil: மண்டல நிறைந்த மாசின் மதிப்புடை வியாழம் போன்றோர்
குண்டல மிலங்க நின்ற கொடியினைக் குறுகித் தோழி
விண்டலர் கோதை விம்மும் விரைகுழ றொழுது நீவிப்
பண்டியல் மணங்க ளெல்லாம் பரிவறப் பணிந்து சொன்னாள்.
reading: Her companion comes up to the creeper-like girl whose earrings shine like Jupiter beside the full moon, bows, strokes her fragrant hair and, with deference, tells her all the marriage customs of old.
nuance: Line 1's comparison (மண்டல நிறைந்த மாசின் மதிப்புடை வியாழம்) is read as the earring beside her moon face; the line could also describe the companion.
event: The companion bows to the princess and speaks to her of the old forms of marriage.

tamil: எரிமணி நெற்றி வேய்ந்த விளம்பிறை யிதுகொ லென்னப்
புரிமணி சுமந்த பொற்பூண் பொறுக்கலா நுசுப்பிற் பாவை
திருமணி வீணைக் குன்றத் திழிந்ததீம் பாலை நீத்தத்
தருமுடி யரச ராழ்வ ரம்மனை யறிவ லென்றாள்.
reading: The companion tells the girl, whose jewelled brow is like the young crescent and whose waist cannot bear her ornaments, that the crowned kings will drown in the flood of sweet paalai melody pouring down from her gem vina as from a hill: 'lady, I know it.'
nuance: அறிவல் makes the forecast a certainty in the companion's mouth; the patikam has already told that the princess is the one who loses.
event: The companion predicts that every royal suitor will be beaten by the princess's playing.

tamil: மண்ணிட மலிர வெங்கு மாந்தரும் வந்து தொக்கா
ரொண்ணிற வுரோணி யூர்ந்த வொளிமதி யொண்பொ னாட்சித்
தெண்ணிற விசும்பி னின்ற தெளிமதி முகத்து நங்கை
கண்ணிய வீணை வாட்போர்க் கலாமின்று காண்டு மென்றே.
reading: People gather from everywhere until the ground overflows, saying 'today we shall see the vina sword-fight of the maiden whose face is like the clear moon in the sky, the moon that rode with Rohini.'
nuance: வீணை வாட்போர் names the music contest as a duel with swords, the figure 628 takes up with யாழ்ப் படை.
event: Crowds gather to watch the contest.

tamil: பசுங்கதிர்க் கடவுள் யோகம் பழிப்பற நுனித்து வல்லான்
விசும்பிவர் கடவு ளொப்பான் விரிச்சிக னறிந்து கூற
வசும்புதே னலங்க லைம்பா லரிவையொ டாய்ந்து நாய்கன்
விசும்புபோன் மாந்த ரார விழுநிதி சிதறி னானே.
reading: When the omen-reader, a man like the gods in the sky who has examined without fault the moon's conjunction, has read and declared the hour, the merchant consults with the lady of honeyed garland and scatters great wealth until people are as full as the sky.
nuance: விரிச்சிகன் is read as one who reads omens (விரிச்சி); the அரிவை he consults is taken as his wife, though the verse does not name her.
event: An astrologer fixes the auspicious hour and the merchant, after consulting his wife, gives wealth away.

tamil: வாசநெய் வண்டு மூச மாந்தளிர் விரல்கள் சேப்பப்
பூசிவெள் ளிலோத்தி ரத்தின் பூம்பொருக் கரைத்த சாந்தின்
காசறு குவளைக் காம ரகவிதழ் பயில மட்டித்
தாசறத் திமிர்ந்து மாத ரணிநலந் திகழ்வித் தாரே.
reading: They rub her with scented oil that draws the bees until their tender fingers redden, then smear her with a paste of white lodhra flowers ground fine to make her bright beauty shine.
event: The attendants anoint the princess.

tamil: கங்கையின் களிற்றி னுச்சிக் கதிர்மணிக் குடத்திற் றந்த
மங்கல வாச நன்னீர் மணிநிறங் கழீஇய தொப்ப
நங்கையை நயப்ப வெல்லாம் விரையொடு துவருஞ் சேர்த்தி
யங்கர வல்கு லாளை யாட்டினா ரரம்பை யன்னார்.
reading: The Rambha-like women bathe the maiden of serpent-hood loins in auspicious scented water mixed with perfumes and astringents, as if the gem colour were washed with water brought in gem pots on elephants from the Ganges.
nuance: The bath by elephants with gold pots of Ganges water recalls the lustration of the goddess of fortune, the figure 627 ends on (திருவிற்கோர் திலகம்).
event: The attendants bathe the princess.

tamil: வெண்ணிற மழையின் மின்போல் வெண்டுகிற் கலாபம் வீக்கிக்
கண்ணிற முலையுந் தோளுஞ் சந்தனத் தேய்வை கொட்டித்
தெண்ணிறச் சிலம்பு செம்பொற் கிண்கிணி பாதஞ் சேர்த்திப்
பண்ணிறச் சுரும்பு சூழும் பனிமுல்லைச் சூட்டு வேய்ந்தார்.
reading: They bind a girdle of white silk on her, like lightning in a white cloud, spread sandal paste on her breasts and shoulders, put clear anklets and gold bells on her feet and crown her with a wreath of cool jasmine circled by bees.
event: The attendants dress the princess.

tamil: எரிமணிச் சுண்ண மின்னு மிருஞ்சிலை முத்தஞ் சேர்த்தித்
திருமணி முலையி னெற்றிச் சிறுபுறஞ் செறியத் தீட்டிப்
புரிமணி யாகத் தைதா விரனுதி கொண்டு பூசி
விரிமணி வியப்ப மேனி யொளிவிட்டு விளங்கிற் றன்றே.
reading: They set pearls and a bow of shining gem powder, paint her breasts and back closely, and smear it on with fingertips over her pearl-hung chest, so that her body shines brighter than the gems.
event: The attendants paint and jewel the princess.

tamil: அருங்கயம் விசும்பிற் பார்க்கு மணிச்சிறு சிரலை யஞ்சி
இருங்கயந் துறந்து திங்க ளிடங்கொண்டு கிடந்த நீலம்
நெருங்கிய மணிவிற் காப்ப நீண்டுலாய்ப் பிறழ்வ செங்கேழ்க்
கருங்கய லல்ல கண்ணே எனக்கரி போக்கி னாரே.
reading: Saying 'these are not dark red-streaked carp but blue lilies that left their pond for fear of the kingfisher that watches from the sky and took refuge in the moon, where the gem bow of her brows guards them', they line her eyes with kohl.
nuance: The verse turns down one standard comparison of the eye (கயல், carp) for another (நீலம், blue lily), with the moon her face and the bow her brows; the conceit is the attendants' own speech.
event: The attendants line the princess's eyes with kohl.

tamil: பொருந்துபொற் றூண்கள் நான்கிற் பொலிந்துநூற் புலவர் செந்நா
வருந்தியும் புகழ்த லாகா மரகத மணிசெய் கூடத்
திருந்திளை யார்கள் கோல மிந்திர னிருமித் தாற்போற்
திருந்தச்செய் ததற்பி னங்கை திருவிற்கோர் திலக மொத்தாள்.
reading: In an emerald hall on four gold pillars, which the tongues of learned poets could not praise enough though they strained, the young women adorned her so well it was as if Indra had made her, and after that the maiden was like a tilaka on the goddess of fortune.
event: The adorning of the princess is finished.

tamil: மண்கனை முழவம் விம்ம வரிவளை துவைப்ப வள்வார்க்
கண்கனைந் திடியின் வெம்பிக் கடலென முரச மார்ப்ப
விண்கனிந் துருகு நீர்மை வெள்வளைத் தோளி போந்தாள்
பண்கனிந் துருகு நல்யாழ்ப் படைபொரு துடைக்க லுற்றே.
reading: As the drums of moulded clay boom, conches blare and great drums roar like the sea and thunder, the white-bangled girl, melting as rain melts from the sky, goes out to break her opponents with the good yaazh, whose melody melts in its mode, as her weapon.
nuance: பொருது உடைக்கல் (to fight and shatter) and யாழ்ப் படை (the lute as army or weapon) cast the music contest as war, the language the suitors' introductions used in 613 and 614.
event: The princess sets out for the contest.

tamil: பரந்தொளி யுமிழும் பைம்பொற் கண்ணடி பதாகை தோட்டி
விரிந்திருண் மேயுஞ் செம்பொன் விளக்குவெண் முரசு கும்பஞ்
சுரந்தவெண் மதியைச் சூன்று கதிர்கொண்டு தொகுத்த போலும்
பொருந்துபொற் கதிர்பெய் கற்றை புணர்கயல் போந்த வன்றே.
reading: Ahead go the auspicious things: gold mirrors spreading light, banners, the goad, red-gold lamps that graze the darkness, the white drum, the full pot, and the paired fish emblem with a gold fringe of rays as though gathered from the white moon.
nuance: The list (mirror, banner, goad, lamp, drum, pot, paired fish) is the set of auspicious objects carried before a bride or a royal; the verse does not number them.
event: The auspicious emblems are carried in procession before the princess.

tamil: வென்றவ னகலம் பூட்ட விளங்கொளி மணிசெய் செப்பி
னின்றெரி பசும்பொன் மாலை போந்தது நெறியிற் பின்ன
ரொன்றிய மணிசெய் நல்யாழ் போந்தன வுருவ மாலை
தின்றுதே னிசைகள் பாடத் திருநகர் சுடர வன்றே.
reading: Next the gold garland to be put on the victor's chest comes out in a shining gem casket, and after it the jewelled yaazhs, garlands whose honey the singing bees drink, and the city blazes with light.
nuance: The garland is for வென்றவன், whoever wins: the procession carries the prize before the outcome is known.
event: The victor's garland and the contest lutes are carried in procession.

reading: With necklaces swinging and garments slipping, swinging their arms valiantly, dwarfs and hunchbacks walk ahead of the bangled maiden like walking toads.
nuance: The metre changes here to a shorter line, which runs through 635.
event: Dwarfs and hunchbacks walk before the princess.

reading: A thousand and eight women with round spears, bodices on long breasts and silk bound at the hips, with quivers full of arrows, bows and swords, go ahead.
event: A guard of a thousand and eight armed women goes before the princess.

reading: Hiding their swelling breasts under bodices, light as arrows, in men's dress, holding gold shields and swords, they serve the golden doll and go before her.
event: The armed women in men's dress escort the princess.

reading: When the crowding guards strike with bamboo staffs crying 'by order, by order, move away', the eyes of the adorned city, in their longing to see, press in all the closer as if saying 'today the order is ours'.
nuance: The answering cry ஆணையின்று எமதே is given to the eyes (கண்ணெருக்குற்றவே) rather than to the people, and can also be read 'no order binds us'.
event: The guards try to clear the crowd, which presses in to see the princess.

reading: Those who scold the guards, 'was the eye born with us for anything but to see her beauty?', throng so close there is no room even to count them, as if heaven and earth had come to a feast.
nuance: The crowd's retort makes seeing beauty the purpose the eye is born for, the view the renunciant of Naladiyar 44 calls blindness.
event: The crowd protests against the guards and packs the street.

tamil: இனஞ்சேரா வாகி விளையோ ருயிரின்மே லெண்ணங் கொள்வான்
புனஞ்சேர் கொடிமுல்லை பூம்பவளத் துட்புக்குப் பூத்த போலும்
வனஞ்சேர் துவர்ச்செவ்வாய் வாளெயிறுங் கண்மலரும் வனைய லாகாக்
கனஞ்சேர் கதிர்முலையுங் கண்டார்கள் வீட்டுலகங் காணார் போலும்!
reading: Her coral mouth, where jasmine seems to have flowered, with its bright teeth, her flower eyes and her heavy breasts, which stand apart from all their kind and set their thought on young men's lives: those who saw them, it seems, will never look upon the world of release.
nuance: The narrator's closing hyperbole makes her beauty a threat to the onlookers' lives and to their release; in a work that ends with its hero renouncing women for release, the line names the stake the story will later settle.

title: காந்தருவதத்தையார் இலம்பகம் 637-660 (7/15)
theme: At the vina contest the assembled kings gaze on Gandharvadattai and speak of her as Death and goddess, vowing war or penance if they lose; she enters, plays and sings three spring songs of a cuckoo's estranged mate won back, her friend the pedi Vinapati announces the terms and jests with the crowd, and when the suitors play in turn the birds that fell entranced at her song fly off at theirs.
source_issues: 652 and 653 have five lines; in each the fifth line repeats the fourth's close with a variant epithet (பேடியோ, எழினி சேர்ந்தாள்), which reads as a refrain of the stanza form rather than an intrusion, but the count is irregular.
637 and 653: the ோ் for ேர் TSCII repair (lines 1, 3, 4 of 637; 4 and 5 of 653) has been accepted as printed by show.
646 and 647 were printed in eight half-lines and joined into four by the build.
656 ends with a doubled full stop (தீந்தவே..).
641 line 4 (மெலிய வாலி விடுக்குமற் றென்மரும்) does not parse with confidence; the word division may be at fault.

cast.role: the Vidyadhara king's daughter, who will wed the one who defeats her at the vina
Gandharvadattai's friend, a pedi (பேடி), who announces the contest
the kings and young men gathered to contend for her at the vina
those in the hall who see her and speak of her
the young women who serve Gandharvadattai, prepare her seat and draw the screen

tamil: மீன்சேர் குழாமனைய மேகலையும் வெம்முலையுங் கூற்றங் கூற்ற
மூன்சே ருயிருய்யக் கொண்டோடிப் போமின்க ளுரைத்தே மென்று
கான்சேர் கமழ்கோதை காறொடர்ந்து கைவிடா தரற்று கின்ற
தேன்சேர் திருவடிமேற் கிண்கிணிபொன் னாவதற்கே தக்க தென்பார்.
reading: Onlookers say her girdle, like a shoal of fish, and her hot breasts are Death upon Death, and bid the suitors run off saving the lives within them, adding that the anklet-bells on her honeyed feet, which the scented garland trails after and will not let go, were fit only to be made of gold.
nuance: The warning, 'we have told you' (உரைத்தேம்), is given before the contest: those who will lose at the vina are told in advance that the prize itself kills. Who speaks is known only from என்பார்; the line could also be read as the suitors' banter among themselves.

tamil: கள்வாய்ப் பெயப்பட்ட மாலைக் கருங்குழல்கள் கண்டார் நைய
வுள்வாய்ப் பெயப்பட்ட வெம்மதுச்செப் போரிணைமெல் லாக மீன்ற
புள்வாய் மணிமழலைப் பொற்சிலம்பி னிக்கொடியை யீன்றாள் போலுங்
கொள்வா னுலகுக்கோர் கூற்றீன்றா ளம்மவோ கொடிய வாறே.
reading: Those who see her say that her mother, in bearing this golden-anklet creeper with the prattling voice of a bird, seems to have borne a Death to take the world, and cry out at how cruel it is.
nuance: The praise goes by way of blame of the mother: bearing a beauty is called bearing Death (கூற்றீன்றாள்), so the crowd's wonder is voiced as reproach.

reading: The garlanded kings, in doubt, ask whether she is Tiru on the red lotus, a Vidyadhara woman of fierce glance, or a daughter of the spotless gods.
nuance: All three guesses are divine or semi-divine; the second, விச்சாதரி, is in fact true of her by birth, since she is the Vidyadhara king's daughter, so the kings' doubt hits the fact without knowing it.

reading: Some kings say that unless it is they who win at the vina and lie on her breasts, they will plunge into a war of bent bows if another takes her, and failing that will do great penance.
nuance: Two fallbacks are named for defeat, war and penance (நற்றவம்); the contest is already shadowed by the threat that its result will be fought over, and தவம் stands here as a disappointed lover's recourse, not as a turn from desire.

reading: Other kings say her lined breasts, like vermilion caskets, torment them, that she has drawn and shot them with her fine eyes, that they cannot live, and that the slender one will now let loose their end.
nuance: The sense of line 4 (மெலிய வாலி விடுக்குமற்று) is not secure; the reading as 'the slender one lets fly' carries the eye-as-archer image of line 3 forward.

reading: Others, with melted hearts, join their palms in worship and wander, saying that she has stretched out her lac-red feet onto soft flowers, shown her beauty and killed them.
nuance: The suitors worship (கைதொழுது) her as one worships a deity while accusing her of murder: the posture of devotion and the charge of killing are the same gesture.

tamil: திங்கண் மதிமுகத்த சேலும் பவளமுஞ் சிலையு முத்துங்
கொங்குண் குழலாண்மெல் லாகத்த கோங்கரும்புங் கொழிப்பில் பொன்னு
மங்கை குழியா வரக்கீத்த செந்தளிர்நெய் தோய்த்த போலு
மங்கை மலரடியுந் தாமரையே யாமறியே மணங்கே யென்பார்.
reading: Others list her parts as fish, coral, bow and pearls in a moon face, kongu buds and unworked gold on her chest, hands like red shoots dipped in ghee and feet like lotus, and say they cannot tell, she is a goddess who afflicts.

tamil: பொன்மகரம் வாய்போழ்ந்த முத்தநூ றோள்யாப்பிற் பொலிந்த வாறு
மின்மகரங் கூத்தாடி வில்லிட் டிருங்குழைக்கீ ழிலங்கு மாறு
மன்மகர வெல்கொடியான் மால்கொள்ளக் கால்கொண்ட முலையி னாளை
யென்னரம்பை யென்னாவா றென்பா ரிமைக்குங்கண் ணிவையோ வென்பார்.
reading: Seeing the pearl strings from golden makara clasps on her shoulders and the lightning-like makara earrings dancing, some ask how she, whose breasts infatuated Kama himself, is not Rambha, and others ask whether these blinking eyes can be hers.
nuance: The blink (இமைக்குங்கண்) is the test: the gods are the unblinking ones (இமையார், 647), so the eyes that blink tell the doubters that the goddess-like woman is mortal after all.

tamil: கோள்வயிர நீளருவிக் குன்றிவர்ந்த செஞ்சுடர்போற் கொலைவேன் மன்னர்
நீள்வயிர வெண்மருப்பி னீலக் களிற்றின்மே னிரைத்தார் பொங்கத்
தோள்வயிரந் தோன்றத் தொழுவா ரழுதுநைவார் தொக்கோர் கோடி
வாள்வயிரம் விற்கு மடநோக்கி யார்கொலோ பெறுவ ரென்பார்.
reading: Kings with murderous spears, high on blue elephants with long white tusks like red flames climbing a hill of diamond streams, their garlands heaving, worship, weep and waste, a crore of them gathered, asking who will win the girl whose eyes outdo the sharpness of swords.
nuance: A crore (கோடி) is the poet's hyperbole for the crowd; the warlike picture of the first two lines gives way to tears in the third.
event: The assembled kings, mounted on elephants, weep and ask who will win her.

tamil: பைம்பொன் நிமிர்கொடி பாவை வனப்பென்னுந் தளிரை ஈன்று
செம்பொன் மலர்ந்திளையார் கண்ணென்னுஞ் சீர்மணிவண் டுழலச் சில்லென்
றம்பொற் சிலம்பரற்ற அன்னம்போல் மெல்லவே ஒதுங்கி அம்பூஞ்
செம்பொற் புரிசை அடைந்தாள்செந் தாமரைமேற் றிருவோ டொப்பாள்.
reading: Like a gold creeper that puts forth the shoot of a doll's beauty, while the young men's eyes roam round her like bees and her anklets tinkle, she walks softly as a swan and reaches the golden enclosure, like Tiru on the red lotus.
event: Gandharvadattai walks to the golden enclosure of the contest hall.

tamil: பட்டியன்ற கண்டத் திரைவளைத்துப் பன்மலர்நன் மாலை நாற்றி
விட்டகலாச் சாந்தி னிலமெழுகி மென்மலர்கள் சிதறித் தூம
மிட்டிளைய ரேத்த விமையார் மடமகள்போ லிருந்து நல்யாழ்
தொட்டெழீஇப் பண்ணெறிந்தாள் கின்னரரு மெய்ம்மறந்து சோர்ந்தா ரன்றே.
reading: With silk screens set round, garlands hung, the floor smeared with sandal, flowers strewn and incense raised, and young women praising, she sits like a daughter of the unblinking gods, takes up her yazh and plays a mode, and even the kinnaras swoon, forgetting themselves.
nuance: The kinnaras are the gods' own musicians; their swoon puts her playing above the celestial standard before any suitor has touched a string.
event: Her maids prepare the screened seat, and Gandharvadattai plays a mode on the yazh.

reading: In her song, when the cuckoo's back is buried in kanji pollen, his young mate takes him for a parrot and shrinks away, and he calls in a voice that melts the bones, shakes out his wings and embraces her: young spring has come.
nuance: The first of three refrain songs (தலைவந்த திளவேனில்) in a new metre; 651 confirms that she has sung them.

reading: In the second song the cock, having bathed in cool kanji pollen, hides his own colour, his mate mistakes him for a parrot and moves off, and the young cock with fine down calls with his gaze and enfolds her with his wing: young spring has come.

In the third song, when the short-legged cock cuckoo comes dusted with pollen and his mate turns from him in dislike, he will not let it be, ruffles his wings, coaxes her back to joy and bows at her feet with his body: young spring has come.
nuance: Across the three songs the mate's estrangement is a mistake about appearance, and it is ended each time by the male's voice and, in the last, by his bowing at her feet; sung by a woman who will give herself only to the one who beats her in music, the songs set out the terms of her contest.

tamil: தளையவிழ் கோதை பாடித் தானமர்ந் திருப்பத் தோழி
விளைமதுக் கண்ணி வீணா பதியெனும் பேடி வேற்க
ணிளையவள் பாட வீர ரெழால்வகை தொடங்க லன்றேல்
வளையவ ளெழாலின் மைந்தர் பாடுக வல்லை யென்றாள்.
reading: When the garlanded singer had sung and sat at ease, her friend Vinapati, a pedi with honey-sweet eyes, called out that the heroes should begin to play the yazh while the young spear-eyed one sang, or else the men should quickly sing to the bangled one's yazh.
nuance: பேடி names one of neither sex; the friend who announces the rules of a contest of men for a woman is herself outside that contest.
event: Vinapati announces the terms: the suitors are to play while Gandharvadattai sings, or sing while she plays.

reading: When some say her shoulders are bamboo, her brow a bow, her mouth coral, her body a mango shoot, and that bearing those breasts is a sickness to her, those sitting near exclaim, 'What, is this one a pedi?', is the girl with the gem girdle a pedi?
nuance: The praise seems to be of Vinapati, whose womanly beauty makes the bystanders doubt what they have been told of her; the refrain line repeats the question. Who is praised is not stated.

reading: She answers the men in leaf-shaped ornaments that the gods, in a clamour, hid her breasts away because her eyes were already a noose that takes its offering and will not go, and a Death that eats lives by sound, and with that she went to the screen.
nuance: Read as Vinapati's reply to 652, the jest turns her lack into a boast: breasts were not needed where the eyes already kill. The speaker is inferred from the sequence, and the image of eyes killing 'by sound' (ஒலிகொண்டு) is not clear.
event: Vinapati answers the onlookers' question with a jest and withdraws to the screen.

reading: She of the waist that can be known only if someone says it is there, under fine silk on wide hips and bending breasts, a creeper of love, carrying the yazh, swayed like a vine through their throng.
nuance: Who carries the yazh is not named; the verse may still be about Vinapati after 653, but 655 to 656 have Gandharvadattai take her seat with the yazh, so it is read as her.
event: Carrying the yazh, she moves through the throng to her place.

reading: As the young women with parrot voices slowly drew back the screen of the crystal-bright gem wall, she went up onto her seat, while her anklet-bells cried in pity as if grieving that the lives of men would vanish today.
event: The maids draw back the screen and Gandharvadattai takes her seat.

reading: With a light-veiling gem wall between, she with eyes like a sword drawn from its sheath sits on this side holding the yazh, and on that side the garlands of the men with blood-stained spears wither.
nuance: The withering garland is the warriors' sign of defeat before any note is struck; the spears are bloody (கறைகெழு) but useless here.
event: Gandharvadattai sits with the yazh behind the gem wall facing the suitors.

reading: Like a divine image with a brow like a bow, she played with all the art and sang, and the bent trees of the leafy grove put out tender shoots and the birds forgot themselves and fell to the ground.
event: Gandharvadattai plays and sings; trees bud and birds fall entranced.

tamil: கருங்கொடிப் புருவ மேறா கயனொடுங் கண்ணு மாடா
வருங்கடி மிடறும் விம்மா தணிமணி யெயிறுந் தோன்றா
விருங்கடற் பவளச் செவ்வாய் திறந்திவள் பாடி னாளோ
நரம்பொடு வீணை நாவி னடந்ததோ வென்று நைந்தார்.
reading: Her dark brows did not rise, her eyes did not move, her throat did not swell, her teeth did not show; the listeners, melting, asked whether she had opened her coral mouth to sing at all, or whether the strung vina had walked upon her tongue.
nuance: Mastery is marked by the absence of effort on the face, so that voice and instrument cannot be told apart.

reading: It is said that when the men, like Ananga himself in skill of music and without fault, took up their great golden yazhs and played and sang, the birds took fright and flew up into the wide sky as if laughing at them.
nuance: The praise of the suitors (வசைத்திறமிலாதவர்) is turned by the birds' mockery (அசிப்ப போன்று), and என்பவே keeps the poet at the distance of report.
event: The suitors play and sing in turn, and the birds fly off in fright.

reading: The listening kinnara birds that came when the girl stroked her yazh turned back at the music of the men's hands: when she sang they came in, and when the garlanded men sang they went away.
event: The kinnara birds come to her singing and leave at the suitors'.

title: காந்தருவதத்தையார் இலம்பகம் 661-684 (8/15)
theme: Gandharvadattai defeats kings, Vedic Brahmins and learned merchants at the vina, and Kattiyankaran says only Kama could win her; Civakan resolves to enter, but a palace woman brings Kantukkatan a hidden letter warning that the king means to kill him, and Kantukkatan begins the story behind the king's rage: at a staged dance Civakan adorned the dancer Anangamaalai, the crowd was undone by her, and she sent him her love by her eyes.
source_issues: Verses 661 line 3, 669 line 1, 673 line 3, 674 line 3 and 678 line 4 carry repairs of conversion slips (FLAG repaired); the repaired readings make sense.
Verses 680, 681 and 682 were printed in eight half-lines and joined into four; the joins look right.
Verse 674 line 4 prints the word division oddly (னனங்கன ன்னான், for அனங்கன் அன்னான்); 679 line 2 (சிறுநுசுப் பொன் றுண்டே) is also oddly divided.
Verse 672 line 4 ends with a doubled full stop.
Verse 667 does not say who or what the sixty-four (அறுபத்து நால்வர்) are.
Verse 671's hearer is named only by a riddling epithet (வேலைநெய் பெய்த திங்கள் விரவிய பெயரினான்) not resolved in these verses.
Verse 684 names no speaker.

cast.role: the hero, raised by the merchant Kantukkatan; here called சீவக சாமி and ஐயன்
the Vidyadhara princess who defeats all comers at the vina (named here only as கோதை, மடந்தை)
the usurping king of Rajamapuram
kings who came seeking the princess
Brahmins skilled in music who contest the princess after the kings
merchants learned in music theory who contest the princess
Civakan's younger brother (named here only as தம்பி)
Civakan's companions
Civakan's companion who carries his message to Kantukkatan
the merchant who raised Civakan (கந்துகன், நாய்கன்)
a woman from the palace who brings a secret warning hidden in a flower
the dancer whom Civakan adorns and who falls in love with him
the audience at the dance

reading: After the kings have lost to the long-haired girl who is so hard to win, men of the way bounded by the four Vedas, practised in the strings and the clear-voiced note, come forward to contest with her.
nuance: The Brahmins are defined at once by Veda and by music: the contest is open to learning, not only to royal birth.
event: With the kings defeated, Vedic Brahmins skilled in music enter the vina contest.

tamil: திருமலர்க் கமலத் தங்கட் டேனின முரல்வ தொப்ப
விரிமலர்க் கோதை பாட வெழால்வகை வீரர் தோற்றார்
எரிமலர்ப் பவளச் செவ்வா யின்னரம் புளர மைந்தர்
புரிநரம் பிசைகொள் பாட லுடைந்தனர் பொன்ன னாட்கே.
reading: As bees hum in a lotus, the garlanded girl sings and the heroes of the எழால் kind of music are beaten; when her coral lips and fingers sound the sweet strings, the young men's songs on twisted strings break down before her.
nuance: எழால் is a technical word of the lute tradition; whether it names a mode, a kind of instrument or a class of performer is not clear from the verse alone.
event: Gandharvadattai sings and plays, and the contestants' music fails against hers.

tamil: வாலரக் கெறிந்த காந்தண் மணியரும் பனைய வாகிக்
கோல்பொரச் சிவந்த கோலக் குவிவிரன் மடந்தை வீணை
நூல்பொரப் புகுந்த நுண்ணூல் வணிகருந் தொலைந்து மாதோ
கால்பொரக் கரிந்த காமர் பங்கயப் பழன மொத்தார்.
reading: Her curled fingers, reddened by the plectrum like kanthal buds stained with lac, defeat even the merchants learned in the fine treatise who came to match her vina by the book, and they wilt like a lotus field scorched by the wind.
nuance: The sequence of losers (kings in 661, Brahmins, now merchants versed in நூல்) runs through the orders of society, so that Civakan, the merchant's foster son, enters when every class has failed.
event: Merchants learned in music theory contest Gandharvadattai and are beaten.

tamil: மூனுயர் நுதிகொள் வேலீ ரொழிகவீங் கில்லை யென்றான்
reading: Kattiyankaran tells the spear-bearing suitors to give up: the one who could beat her at the sweet makara-headed vina would be Kama himself, whose long bow withers the strength of the mighty, and no such one is here.
event: Kattiyankaran declares that no one present can defeat the princess and tells the suitors to stop.

tamil: மறுமுயற் கிவர்ந்த வேக மாசுண மடையப் பட்ட
நிறைமதி போன்று மன்னர் ஒளிகுறைந் துருகி நைய
வறுபகல் கழிந்த பின்றை யந்நகர்க் காதி நாய்கன்
சிறுவனோர் சிங்க வேற்றை சீவக சாமி யென்பான்,
reading: As the kings dim and melt like the full moon caught by the swift serpent that leaps at its hare, six days pass, and then the son of the city's chief merchant, a lion among young men called Civaka Sami, comes into the story.
nuance: The verse is the first half of a sentence that runs into 666; Civakan is introduced by his foster father's rank (ஆதி நாய்கன் சிறுவன்), not by his royal birth.
event: The kings lose heart, and after six days Civakan is introduced as the next contender.

tamil: தம்பியுந் தோழன் மாருந் தானுமற் றெண்ணிச் சூழ்ந்து
வெம்பிய வீணைப் போருட் செல்குவம் யாமு முன்னே
தும்பறப் புத்தி சேன சொல்லிது குரவற் கென்ன
கந்துகற் கவனுஞ் சொன்னா னவனிது விளம்பி னானே.
reading: Civakan, his younger brother and his companions take counsel and resolve to go first into the fierce vina contest; he asks Buddhisenan to tell this to the elder, Buddhisenan tells Kantukkatan, and Kantukkatan answers.
nuance: The decision passes through the foster father before it is acted on: the hero does not go to the contest without the elder's word.
event: Civakan resolves with his brother and friends to enter the contest and sends word through Buddhisenan to Kantukkatan.

tamil: ஐயனுக் கமைந்த நீரா ரறுபத்து நால்வ ரம்பொன்
வையகத் தமிர்த மன்னார் வாக்கமை பாவை யொப்பா
ரெய்திய விளமை மிக்கா ரியைந்தன ரென்று பின்னுங்
கையமை சிலையி னாற்குக் கந்துக னிதுவுங் கூறும்.
reading: Kantukkatan says that sixty-four of a nature fitting for the master, like nectar on earth and like finely made figures, in the fullness of youth, have come together; and further he tells the bowman something more.
nuance: Who or what the sixty-four (அறுபத்து நால்வர்) are is not settled by the verse: the figures of nectar, statues and ripe youth suit women, but the number is that of the arts, and the verse may say that all sixty-four have gathered in the master.
event: Kantukkatan replies to the message and turns to tell Civakan something more.

tamil: மறைவல்லாற் குரைக்கும் போழ்திற் கோயிலு ணின்று மாலைப்
பிறைவெல்லும் நுதலி னாளோர் பெண்கொடி வந்து கூந்த
லுறைசெல நீக்கிப் பைந்தா ளொண்மணிக் குவளை நீட்ட
நறைவெல்லும் நாக மாலை நோக்கொடு பூக்கொண் டானே.
reading: While he is speaking to the learned one, a woman with a brow that outshines the crescent comes from the palace, slips her hair from its sheath and holds out a blue kuvalai on its green stalk, and he takes the flower with a look.
nuance: Neither who is addressed as மறைவல்லான் nor who takes the flower is named here; 669 shows that the merchant is the one who reads what it hides.
event: A woman from the palace brings Kantukkatan a blue lily as a covert sign.

tamil: நல்லவ ணோக்க நாய்கன் றேர்ந்துபூங் குவளைப் போதி
னல்லியுட் கிடந்த வோலை தாளது சலாகை யாதல்
சொல்லுமென் றாய்ந்து கொண்டு துகிலிகைக் கணக்கு நோக்கி
வல்லிதிற் சலாகை சுற்றி யோலையை வாசிக் கின்றான்.
reading: Seeing her meaning, the merchant searches the flower and finds a palm-leaf letter lying among its petals with the stalk serving as its stylus; he takes it, works out the painter's cipher, unrolls it around the stylus and reads.
nuance: The letter is in a cipher (துகிலிகைக் கணக்கு), so the warning comes from someone inside the palace who must hide it from the king.
event: Kantukkatan finds a secret letter in the flower and reads it.

tamil: நம்பனை நகரி னீக்கிச் சேமத்தால் வைக்க தீயுட்
செம்பொன்போற் பெரிதுஞ் சேந்து செகுத்திட லுற்று நின்றான்
வெம்பினான் காரி யுண்டிக் கடவுளிற் கனன்று வேந்தன்
இம்பரின் றெனக்குச் சொன்னா னிதுபட்ட தடிகள் என்றாள்.
reading: The message: take the noble one out of the city and keep him safe, for the king, reddened like gold in fire, stands ready to kill him, burning in anger like the god who swallowed poison; the king said so to me today, and this is what has happened, sir.
nuance: The verse ends in என்றாள், so the woman voices the warning; how much of it is the letter's text and how much her own report is not marked. The god compared to the angry king is named only as the one who ate the poison.
event: The palace woman warns Kantukkatan that the king means to kill Civakan and urges him to send Civakan out of the city.

tamil: ஓலையை யவட்கு நீட்டி யொண்மணிக் குழையு முத்தும்
மாலையும் படுசொ லொற்றி வம்மென மறைய நல்கி
வேலைநெய் பெய்த திங்கள் விரவிய பெயரி னாற்கு
மேலைநாட் பட்ட தொன்று விளம்புவல் கேளி தென்றான்.
reading: Handing the letter back to her, he gives her in secret a gem earring, pearls and a garland as tokens, seals the message and bids her come again; then to the one whose name joins the moon with the sea's nectar he says he will tell something that happened in earlier days.
nuance: The hearer is named by a riddling epithet (வேலைநெய் பெய்த திங்கள் விரவிய பெயரினான்) that the verse does not resolve; since Civakan himself took part in the episode now told, the hearer may be someone else.
event: Kantukkatan rewards the messenger secretly and begins to tell of a past event.

tamil: கடியரங் கணிந்து மூதூர்க் கடல்கிளர்ந் தனைய தொப்ப
நடையறி புலவ ரீண்டி நாடக நயந்து காண்பான்
குடையுடை யவனொ டெண்ணிச் சீவகற் கொணர்மி னென்னத்
தொடையல்சூழ் வேலி னானுந் தோழருங் காணச் சென்றார்..
reading: When the old city, decked for the festival hall, surged like the sea and poets who knew the art of the stage crowded in, someone who wished to see a drama took counsel with the umbrella-bearing king and had Civakan sent for, and the spear-bearer and his friends went to watch.
nuance: Who proposes the summons is left unnamed; the verse says only that it was agreed with the king, which matters for the king's later rage in 670.
event: At a staged performance before the king, Civakan is summoned and goes with his friends to watch.

tamil: நிலமறிந் தணிக வையன் சீவகன் நெறியி னென்ன
நலநுதற் பட்டங் கட்டி நகைமுடிக் கோதை சூட்டி
யலர்முலைக் குருதிச் சாந்து மாரமும் பூணுஞ் சேர்த்திக்
reading: Told to adorn the dancer as the rules of the stage require, Master Civakan ties the band on her fine brow, crowns her with a garland, puts blood-red sandal, a necklace and jewels on her breasts, and fits her with a skirt of red silk.
nuance: The adornment is a learned skill (நிலமறிந்து, நெறியின்): Civakan is shown as master of the stage arts, and the same act sets the dancer's love in motion.
event: Civakan adorns the dancer for the performance.

tamil: திருவிலே சொரிந்து மின்னுங் குண்டலஞ் செம்பொ னோலை
யுருவுகொண் மதிய மன்ன வொளிமுகஞ் சுடர வாக்கிப்
பரியகஞ் சிலம்பு செம்பொற் கிண்கிணி பாதஞ் சேர்த்தி
யரிவையை யரம்பை நாண வணிந்தன னனங்கன ன்னான்.
reading: The one like Anangan sets flashing earrings and gold ear-rolls so that her moon-like face shines, and puts anklet, foot-ring and gold bells on her feet, adorning the woman until Rambha would be ashamed.
nuance: Calling the adorner அனங்கன் (Kama) here answers Kattiyankaran's claim in 664 that only Kama could win the princess.
event: Civakan finishes adorning the dancer.

tamil: தோற்பொலி முழவும் யாழும் துளைபயில் குழலு மேங்கக்
காற்கொசி கொம்பு போலப் போந்துகைத் தலங்கள் காட்டி
மேற்பட வெருவி நோக்கித் தானைய விட்டிட் டொல்கித்
தோற்றினாள் முகஞ்செய் கோலந் துளக்கினாண் மனத்தை யெல்லாம்.
reading: As skin drum, yazh and pierced flute sound, she comes on like a twig bending in the wind, shows her hand gestures, looks up as if startled, lets her garment trail and sways; the face she has made up shakes every mind.
event: The dancer enters and begins her dance to drum, lute and flute.

tamil: தெண்மட்டுத் துவலை மாலை தேனொடு துளிப்பத் திங்க
ளுண்ணட்ட குவளை போலு முருவக்கண் வெருவி யாட
விண்விட்டுக் கடவுள் வீழ நுடங்கின புருவ நெஞ்சம்
பண்விட்ட திருந்து காணும் பன்மணிக் கழலி னார்க்கே.
reading: Her eyes, like kuvalai planted in the moon, dart as if in fear, her garland drips honey, and her brows bend so that gods would fall from the sky; and the hearts of the jewel-anklet men who sit watching lose their tune.
event: The dancer's eyes and brows move as she dances, and the watchers are overcome.

tamil: செங்கதிர்ச் சிலம்பு செம்பொற் கிண்கிணி சிலம்பக் கோதை
பொங்கப்பொன் னோலை வட்டம் பொழிந்துமின் னுகுப்பப் போர்த்த
குங்குமச் சாந்து வேய்ந்து குண்டலந் திருவில் வீச
வங்கதி ரார மின்ன வரிவைகூத் தாடு கின்றாள்.
reading: With anklet and gold bells ringing, her garland swelling, the gold ear-disc showering lightning, saffron paste spread on her, earrings flashing like a rainbow and her necklace gleaming, the woman dances.
event: The dancer dances in full ornament.

tamil: மருங்குலு மொன்று தாய்க்கு மொருமக ளாத லோர்ந்து
மிரும்பினா லியன்ற நெஞ்சத் திவர்களோ விருந்து காண்க
வரங்கின்மே லிவளைத் தந்த தாய் கொலோ கயத்தி யன்றேற்
சுரும்புசூழ் கண்ணி சூட்டி யவர்கொலோ கயவர் செல்லீர்.
reading: Some in the crowd say: knowing her waist is a single thread and she is her mother's only daughter, can these iron-hearted people sit and watch? Was it her base mother who brought her onto the stage, or else the base men who crowned her with the bee-haunted garland? Go away!
nuance: The outrage is praise by hyperbole: the waist is too slender to bear a dance. Its target includes, without naming him, the one who garlanded her in 673, Civakan himself.

tamil: அகிலார் புகையலாற் சாந்தணியாள் பூச்சாரச் செல்லாள் செல்லிற்
பகலே பகைவளர்த்த பாவை சிறுநுசுப் பொன் றுண்டே பாவம்
இகலேந் திளமுலைமேற் சாந்தெழுதி முத்தணிந்து பூவுஞ் சூட்ட
முகிலேந்து மின்மருங்குல் மொய்குழற்றா யிதுகண்டு முளளே பாவம்.
